why.description:
Why explains, as prose, why the scenario exists and what problem it
solves.

points.description: Points are the key points, in display order.

narration.description: Narration is spoken over the briefing.

Briefing.description: Briefing introduces a scenario before its steps, for example on slides that open a video.

body.description:
Body is the request body as JSON, kept byte for byte so key order
survives a round trip.

ExampleRequest.description: ExampleRequest is an illustrative HTTP request.

ExampleResponse.description: ExampleResponse is an illustrative HTTP response.

token.description: Token is the token definition ID.

label.description: Label says where the token travels, such as "Signature-Key header".

header.description: Header and Payload are the decoded JWT header and claims.

ExampleToken.description: ExampleToken is a decoded token carried by a message.

kind.description: Kind classifies the annotation, such as "assertion" or "client-event".

text.description: Text is the annotation as a person reads it.

ok.description: OK is the result of an assertion; unset for other kinds.

time.description:
Time is when the annotated event happened, when it differs from the
exchange's time.

ExchangeAnnotation.description: ExchangeAnnotation is a piece of evidence about an exchange.

Finding.description: Finding is an analysis result attached to a step.

source.description: Source cites where the example comes from, such as "draft-11 §7.2.1".

request.description: Request is the HTTP request, for steps that send one.

response.description: Response is the HTTP response, for steps that return one.

tokens.description: Tokens are decoded tokens the message carries, in display order.

samples.description:
Samples are code that sends or handles this message, such as SDK
calls, shown beside the HTTP form.

note.description: Note explains anything the reader should notice in this example.

FlowExample.description: FlowExample is an illustrative message for one step: the HTTP request, the HTTP response and decoded tokens.

id.description: ID is the unique identifier scenarios refer to.

Group.description: Group is a navigation section that scenarios are listed under.

Narration.description: Narration is text written to be spoken, keyed by BCP 47 language tag.

after_step.description:
AfterStep is the number of the step it followed, or 0 when it came
before the first matched step.

from.description: From and To are the participants, when the binding resolved them.

ObservedExtra.description: ObservedExtra is an observed exchange that matched no step.

from.description: From and To are the capturing tool's labels for sender and receiver.

request_id.description: RequestID is the value of a request ID header, when the capture has one.

tokens.description: Tokens are the tokens found in the message, decoded and not verified.

label.description: Label and Annotations are evidence the capturing tool recorded.

repeats.description: Repeats is how many exchanges a repeated step took, when more than one.

body_truncated.description: BodyTruncated reports that a body was cut at the capture's size limit.

ObservedMessage.description: ObservedMessage is an exchange observed in a real system, shown as a step's example is: request, response and decoded tokens.

scenario.description: Scenario is the ID of the scenario this entry is an instance of.

source.description:
Source names the tool that captured the run; RequestFidelity says
whether its requests are the wire messages or a client's.

instance.description: Instance is this instance's number, from 1, of Instances found.

from.description: From and To bound the instance's exchanges in time.

runner_up.description: RunnerUp is the next-best scenario at this point of the capture.

matched.description:
Counts of step outcomes; Matched counts every matched step and Weak
the matched steps that are weak. Explained counts exchanges matched
to steps and Extra those that matched none.

redacted.description:
Redacted reports that raw token, signature and credential values
were masked.

ObservedRun.description: ObservedRun summarizes one instance of a scenario found in a capture.

OutlineRole.description: OutlineRole is one entity in an outline.

narration.description: Narration replaces the step's narration for this representation.

RepresentationNarration.description: RepresentationNarration overrides a step's narration when the reader views the step in one representation, such as cURL or Go code.

language.description:
Language names the code's language with a common highlighter name,
such as "go", "typescript", "python" or "csharp". Samples are also
representations a step's narration can be overridden for.

label.description:
Label distinguishes samples in one language, such as "Agent" and
"Resource".

role.description: Role is the entity ID whose developer writes this code.

code.description:
Code is inline code, or a source's code once resolved. A sample has
Code, Source, or both.

source.description: Source refers to a marked region of a file in a repository.

Sample.description: Sample is code that sends or handles a step's message, such as a Go SDK call.

repo.description:
Repo is the repository's module-style path, such as
"github.com/aauth-dev/aauth-go".

ref.description:
Ref is a tag or commit to read the file at. Empty reads the
checkout's working tree.

path.description: Path is the file's path within the repository.

region.description: Region is the marked region's name.

SampleSource.description: SampleSource refers to the code between "pidl:begin <region>" and "pidl:end <region>" markers, in comments, in a file of a repository.

name.description: Name is the claim name, such as "aud" or "agent_jkt".

checked_by.description: CheckedBy lists the entities that check this claim.

description.description: Description explains what the claim carries or how it is checked.

TokenClaim.description: TokenClaim is one claim in a token and the entities that check it.

format.description: Format names the format and its major version, "pidl-walkthrough/v1".

language.description: Language is the source language of the narration.

findings.description:
Findings holds findings that do not locate a single flow, such as an
unused role.

Walkthrough.description: Walkthrough is a protocol prepared for step-by-step presentation: roles in entities order and, for each scenario in output order, its steps with fragments expanded in place.

observed_run.description:
ObservedRun is set on a scenario entry that shows a run observed in a
real system: one instance of the scenario found in a capture.

observed_extra.description:
ObservedExtra are the run's exchanges that matched no step, each
placed after the step it followed.

WalkthroughScenario.description: WalkthroughScenario is one scenario with its expanded steps.

number.description: Number is the 1-based position within the expanded scenario.

id.description:
ID is the step's flow ID, qualified as "<include>.<id>" for a step
inside an included fragment; empty when the flow has no ID.

fragments.description: Fragments names the fragments this step sits inside, outermost first.

representations.description: Representations holds narration overrides by representation.

observed.description:
Observed is the exchange a real run produced for this step, in a
scenario entry with an ObservedRun. ObservedStatus is matched,
notSeen, skipped, unmatchable or unobservable; ObservedStrength is
strong or weak for a matched step.

curl.description: Curl is a curl command equivalent to the example request.

WalkthroughStep.description: WalkthroughStep is one message of an expanded scenario.

WalkthroughToken.description: WalkthroughToken is a token definition with the claims its checkers use.

title: PIDL Walkthrough
description: A protocol prepared for step-by-step presentation, produced by `pidl generate -f walkthrough-json`.
